requirements.title: Project and task identity
requirements.requirement: Create a stable task_id and immutable original-request TaskRevision. Preallocate an ANALYZE Run while the candidate specification is still DRAFT; freeze the original request, inputs, model configuration, trusted scope and total budget. Intent parsing, clarification, planning, repair, tools and reporting belong to this same Run. Reject unauthorized creation; deduplicate repeated requests.

requirements.title: Controlled input import
requirements.requirement: Validate source, size, actual format and access. Store immutable original bytes with SHA-256 and acquisition metadata. Download only from configured sources. Reject empty responses, HTML error pages, unsupported formats and unclear permission; never silently replace the file.

requirements.title: Object inventory and preprocessing
requirements.requirement: List model/entity, author and label chain identities, residue and atom counts, insertion codes, missing data and alternate conformers. Record before/after selection changes and whether ligands, waters and ions participate. Stop affected calculations if identity cannot be explained.

requirements.title: Natural language to TaskSpec
requirements.requirement: Within the preallocated Run, derive the goal, objects, selections, fit/evaluation regions, contact definition, units, outputs and constraints. Preserve candidate provenance. Before the first scientific computation, programmatically check and freeze one FrozenTaskSpec with frozen_spec_id; every formal plan references that identity.

requirements.title: Necessary clarification and revision
requirements.requirement: Ask only questions that change scientific meaning. Before freezing, append answers to the same Run without rewriting the original request, extending its deadline or resetting its budget. After freezing, a changed goal, object, selection or method creates a linked new TaskRevision and Run; preserve all old costs and unresolved state.

requirements.title: Available capability catalogue
requirements.requirement: Expose scientific purpose, preconditions, typed I/O, version, resource class and validated range. Keep registration, deployment health, reference-test passage and current authorization separate. A declared interface alone is not READY and must not be offered as executable.

requirements.title: Dependency planning and preflight compilation
requirements.requirement: The model proposes typed steps, dependencies, expected artifacts, validation nodes and stop conditions under the same frozen specification. Deterministically reject cycles, missing references, incompatible types, failed scientific preconditions, denied access and excessive budgets. A PlanRevision may change execution strategy within the same contract, not the scientific question.

requirements.title: Selections and cross-structure mapping
requirements.requirement: Materialize one-to-one atom pairs while retaining author/label namespaces and insertion codes. A frozen sequence correspondence rule may propose the mapping, but expose coverage, conflicts, missing residues and unmatched items. Empty selections, duplicate pairs or unresolved ambiguity block fitting.

requirements.title: Superposition and regional comparison
requirements.requirement: Compute the specified right-handed rigid transform, evaluation-region RMSD and per-pair displacement. Distinguish full-chain fitting, independent fits per region and evaluation after a fixed CORE fit. Record atom pairs and exclusions; do not silently trim outliers. Reject degeneracy, non-finite values and unsupported units.

requirements.title: Geometric contacts
requirements.requirement: Use the frozen object identities, heavy-atom selection, Euclidean-distance threshold and explicit < or ≤ rule. Return atom pairs and separately deduplicated residue summaries. Do not promote distance contacts into hydrogen bonds, affinity or functional causation without the required evidence.

requirements.title: Controlled real execution
requirements.requirement: Run fixed adapters in restricted Worker environments, with read-only inputs, dedicated outputs and enforced process/network/resource limits. Persist actual Step/Attempt execution facts. Ordinary new immutable artifacts within an authorized project are automatically allowed; the model cannot invent successful files.

requirements.title: Bounded retries and scientific repair
requirements.requirement: Retry only safe transient failures within limits. Append diagnosed PlanRevisions and Attempts under the same FrozenTaskSpec and remaining Run budget. Preserve the goal, acceptance rules, all failed candidates and all costs. Stop when exhausted, stalled, denied or unrecoverable; never relax a threshold merely to obtain a pass.

requirements.title: Query, cancellation and recovery
requirements.requirement: Use server-side facts as the authority; closing a page does not remove the Run. Separate a cancellation request from confirmed termination. Reconcile actual processes/jobs and existing artifacts before resubmitting. Preserve UNKNOWN when the side effect cannot be established.

requirements.title: Execution and scientific acceptance
requirements.requirement: Record execution status independently from scientific_status. Check identity, mapping, units, schema, numerical invariants or independent references, and report citations. Successful process exit does not establish scientific acceptance. Invalid candidates may be shown only with explicit diagnostic labels.

requirements.title: Evidence report and analytical views
requirements.requirement: P0 provides object/mapping tables, metrics, displacement/contact plots and auditable selection manifests. Optional read-only Mol* 3D highlighting is P1. Report the question, objects, method, results, evidence, limits and unfinished parts; populate numerical values from validated artifacts.

requirements.title: Immutable artifacts and downloads
requirements.requirement: Automatically save authorized new project outputs and allow downloads within the same access policy. A reproducibility bundle records input identities, frozen specification, parameters, versions, artifacts and checks. Including original inputs depends on data rights; reject corrupted, missing or no-longer-authorized downloads.

requirements.title: High-impact actions and approval
requirements.requirement: P0 keeps arbitrary code, export, overwriting and real HPC submission disabled rather than displaying nonfunctional approval controls. P1 approval binds the exact actor, project, input hashes, destination, parameters, versions, expiry and one-time use. Approval cannot expand hard permissions, support scope or cumulative hard budget.

requirements.title: Identity, projects and data boundaries
requirements.requirement: A team pilot needs real server-side authentication and per-object authorization across storage, retrieval, state, caches, streams and download. Apply separate policies to private coordinates sent to a model, traces and exports. Model-supplied roles or tenant names confer no authority; connectors keep credentials server-side.

requirements.title: Trace, cost and error ledger
requirements.requirement: From Run creation, retain parsing, clarification, planning, execution, validation and reporting events, structured failures, retries, both outcome types and cumulative resource use. Break down model/tool/failure/retry costs. Mark missing billing UNKNOWN rather than zero; minimize and redact sensitive diagnostics.

requirements.title: Model configuration and planner adapter
requirements.requirement: Use a provider-neutral Planner/ModelAdapter and one initial production configuration. Freeze model/prompt settings before the Run. All model calls, including intent parsing, belong to it. Missing credentials, quota or network must produce an explicit failure; fixed-plan reference mode is visibly separate.

requirements.title: Reproduction and version freeze
requirements.requirement: Publish a machine-readable manifest distinguishing deterministic computations from stochastic model/search choices. Freeze or identify inputs, tool/environment/checker versions and tolerances. Disclose hosted components that cannot be frozen; identify missing material instead of claiming complete reproduction.

requirements.title: Capability packaging and release
requirements.requirement: Ship purpose, preconditions, schemas, limits, adapter, error codes, independent checks, reference tasks and reporting rules together. Enable a capability only after contract, numerical, permission and existing-regression checks pass. Registration is not deployment.

requirements.title: Regression and real-model evaluation
requirements.requirement: First test contracts, numerics and deterministic execution; then test real-model object interpretation, planning, artifacts, explanations, refusal and total cost. Freeze the final test set. Missing Run artifacts remain failures; a broken global reference/scorer makes the evaluation INVALID, rather than making every model answer wrong.

requirements.title: Feedback and failure triage
requirements.requirement: Link feedback to an accessible Run, frozen contract and relevant Attempt/artifact/report version. Creation is NEEDS_REPRODUCTION. Authorized reproduction and scientific review append REPRODUCED, DISPUTED or resolution evidence; confirmed defects link a regression task and fix version. Likes and model self-assessment do not become scientific truth.

acceptance.title: Input and specification contracts
acceptance.pass_rule: Round-trip valid normalized selections; append pre-freeze clarification within one Run; bind frozen_spec_id before scientific execution. Invalid, unknown or non-finite parameters never reach scientific tools.

acceptance.title: Unambiguous structural identity
acceptance.pass_rule: Preserve model, instance, namespace, mapping, counts, exclusions and input hash. Similar numbering or finite output cannot rescue a wrong object.

acceptance.title: Superposition and reference frames
acceptance.pass_rule: Agree with a pre-frozen independent reference within tool-specific tolerances. Record R/t convention, fit region F, evaluation region E and det(R)>0. The AdK full-chain value near 7.130700 Å is one regression fixture only.

acceptance.title: Recomputable contact definition
acceptance.pass_rule: Match atom-pair counts and deduplicated residue counts separately, including units and threshold convention. Do not infer affinity or hydrogen bonds from proximity alone.

acceptance.title: A checker cannot certify itself
acceptance.pass_rule: Block all injected critical defects from trusted delivery. Disclose shared code/reference dependencies between the runtime validator and external acceptance; add independent recalculation for shared critical logic.

acceptance.title: Real-model end-to-end completion
acceptance.pass_rule: Meet frozen quality goals using actual model-selected actions and actual observations. Keep all versions, Attempts, failures and costs. Fixed plans and mock models do not satisfy this gate.

acceptance.title: Ambiguous, invalid and unsupported tasks
acceptance.pass_rule: Ask only decisive questions; apply documented defaults transparently; never invent a capability or silently substitute the goal. Score expected handling against frozen labels.

acceptance.title: Complete denominators and cost
acceptance.pass_rule: Missing artifacts count as failed Runs. Retries add Attempts and cost, not independent samples. Report UNKNOWN costs and coverage. Corrupted global references produce INVALID_EVALUATION.

acceptance.title: Normal outputs proceed automatically
acceptance.pass_rule: Authorized new project artifacts and same-permission downloads require no extra approval. Overwrite/export actions cannot masquerade as normal output, and approval cannot enable disabled P0 actions.

acceptance.title: Real authentication and project isolation
acceptance.pass_rule: Derive actor/project from a trusted server session and authorize every resource. Block cross-project reads, writes and cache borrowing; revoke new access when a session or membership is withdrawn.

acceptance.title: Untrusted data cannot grant capability
acceptance.pass_rule: Retrieved text cannot alter permissions, registry, budgets or approvals. Keep legitimate branches usable when rejecting an unrelated action. Measure task utility and actual unauthorized effects separately.

acceptance.title: Fixed execution entry points and effective isolation
acceptance.pass_rule: No arbitrary shell/eval. Enforce read-only inputs, a dedicated output root, no host credentials, network/resource restrictions and process cleanup. Test path-resolution races, not just strings.

acceptance.title: Atomic cumulative budget
acceptance.pass_rule: The server defines costs and hard limits. Reserve before each action and settle actual use across the entire Run. Resume/replanning cannot reset limits or hide costs; approval cannot override them.

acceptance.title: Stable identities through retry and recovery
acceptance.pass_rule: Reuse the same operation for the same authenticated scope, idempotency key and payload digest; conflict on changed payload. Preserve every Attempt and prevent duplicate accepted publication.

acceptance.title: Cancellation and UNKNOWN reflect execution facts
acceptance.pass_rule: Do not claim termination at request time. Reconcile uncertain effects before resubmission and settle resources after actual process/job cleanup. P0 does not claim verified Slurm recovery.

acceptance.title: Exact high-impact approval
acceptance.pass_rule: Expire approval when a critical field changes; validate approver authority and consume it once. A digest alone grants no authority. Ordinary new reports do not need approval.

acceptance.title: Credentials and data minimization
acceptance.pass_rule: Inject credentials only in controlled connectors. Exclude them from model context, reports, URLs and normal logs. Private model-bound data must satisfy project policy.

acceptance.title: Readable and injection-safe reports
acceptance.pass_rule: Show objects, selections, method, units, results, evidence, exclusions and limits. Clearly label inconclusive science. Escape uploaded text/scripts and expose only authorized completed data.

acceptance.title: Complete provenance and replay
acceptance.pass_rule: Link original TaskRevision, candidate/clarification events, FrozenTaskSpec, PlanRevision and Attempt; retain all critical versions/hashes. Same-contract repair shares a Run; changed science creates a linked new Run. Preserve validation history.

acceptance.title: Extensions preserve existing capabilities
acceptance.pass_rule: Require scientific purpose, preconditions, I/O, permissions, resource/error semantics, validators and reference tasks. Do not offer an unvalidated capability as READY; prevent severe old-task regressions.

acceptance.title: Feedback, release and rollback are exercisable
acceptance.pass_rule: Version code/images/configuration/references and acceptance evidence. Stop on severe scientific error, unauthorized effects or major regressions. Preserve feedback history and in-flight versions; a FIXED issue needs regression/fix references and cannot rewrite old scientific outcomes.

acceptance.title: Performance only under declared load
acceptance.pass_rule: Calibrate and freeze SLOs and hardware after the pilot. P95 acceptance/query latency ≤2 s is a candidate target, excluding model inference and scientific completion; it is not a measured capacity claim.

entities: Project / Membership
Trusted identity, project membership and role
All reads, caches, events and downloads recheck current membership.
Task / TaskRevision
Stable task plus immutable original-request revision
Clarification is an appended Run event. A changed frozen scientific question creates a linked revision and Run.
Run
Preallocated complete analysis episode
Freeze request, inputs, configuration, scope and cumulative budget at creation. Do not create separate planning Runs to reset cost.
FrozenTaskSpec
One immutable scientific definition per analysis Run
Bind before the first scientific TOOL operation. All formal plans, results and validations reference the same frozen_spec_id.
Plan / Step
Immutable versioned dependency plan and logical operations
Compile types, references, DAG, preconditions and authorization. Revisions preserve the frozen scientific contract.
Attempt
An actual MODEL, PREFLIGHT or TOOL execution
Persist operation_id, plan/step binding where required, lease_epoch, actual usage and outcome. A retry is a new Attempt within the same Run.
Job
An external backend execution object reserved for P1
Identify by backend and external job ID plus stable operation correlation. Scheduler disappearance is not terminal-state proof.
Artifact
Immutable input or derived bytes plus provenance
Bind SHA-256, size, media type, project and actual producing Attempt or control event. The model sees artifact IDs, never host paths.
Validation
An appended checker/policy result for an artifact
Bind Run, frozen specification, checker/policy versions, measurements and ACCEPTED/REJECTED/INCONCLUSIVE outcome.
RunEvent / Outbox
Ordered durable facts and pending notifications
Commit state and event atomically. A stream is a projection; network delivery may duplicate.
RunScope / BudgetReservation
Server-derived authorization and resource reservation
Reserve atomically before dispatch, retain unknown liabilities and settle observed usage. Client estimates never grant authority.
ActionIntent / Approval
Reserved exact high-impact action and approval records
P1 only: current approver authority, expiry/revocation, exact binding and atomic one-time consumption.
FeedbackIssue
Versioned user report and reproduction history
Start NEEDS_REPRODUCTION; access-check every reference. Reproduction and domain judgment require authorized evidence.

engineering_chapters.title: From natural-language requests to testable task contracts
engineering_chapters.lead: A mature system must state what it accepted, which object it measured and what evidence will count as completion. Conversation gathers intent; a versioned contract makes it executable and reviewable.
sections: Define the deliverable before the dialogue

“Compare these structures” could mean fold, assembly, local conformation or model quality. Decompose the request into objects, measurements, required inputs and outputs. A useful first operation is a specified-atom comparison under an explicit mapping. The Task persists the formal request after the chat disconnects. Separate user-provided facts, facts confirmed from files and information still unknown. Record defaults and their scientific effect; do not use a convenient chain default to erase ambiguity.
Put scientific semantics in both input and output contracts

A file path is not an input identity. Record content hash, format, model, chain namespace, residue/atom selection, assembly handling, units and missing-data policy. In mmCIF, auth and label identifiers can differ; a syntactically valid chain name may select the wrong entity. First inspect the actual hierarchy. Outputs should include correspondence tables, transformation parameters, per-position differences, coverage, exclusions and a validation record. A low RMSD is not a universal success criterion: it depends on the fitted and evaluated object.
Let the planner propose and the compiler verify

The model selects candidate capabilities and dependencies. A deterministic compiler checks registered tool versions, typed references, compatible selections, required validation, DAG structure, scope and resource limits. Reject a plan before side effects when its prerequisites fail. Accept equivalent valid paths rather than forcing one narrative reference sequence. Keep candidate actions, accepted plans, actual tool results and report explanations as distinct records.
Turn uncertainty into a control branch

Missing decisive identity goes to clarification; unsupported scope goes to a reasoned boundary response; transient tool failure goes to a safe bounded retry; insufficient science goes to rejection or inconclusive evidence. A same-contract execution repair can append a plan version. A changed scientific question after freezing creates a linked new request revision and Run. The original contract and failed evidence remain auditable.
failure: A multichain file returns a plausible numeric result after a default chain was selected.

Reject trusted scientific delivery if the actual selection does not match the contract. Show the object inventory, obtain the decisive selection and preserve the failed attempt. A plausible number does not establish that the intended object was measured.
checklist: A task has explicit objects, supported scope and refusal conditions.
Every default has provenance and a stated effect.
Input/output schemas include units, identity and selection semantics.
Planner proposals cannot bypass deterministic preconditions.
The report can be traced to a frozen contract and actual artifacts.

engineering_chapters.title: Reference architecture and data ownership
engineering_chapters.lead: Separate control, scientific execution and evidence storage so the system can explain results, recover failures and assign responsibility. A single overall status is not enough.
sections: Control and computation are separate responsibilities

The interface/API receives the task, authenticates access and exposes state. The controller assembles context, proposes bounded actions and records decisions. Adapters and Workers run scientific programs in controlled environments. A domain validator checks real objects and outputs; reporting cites the artifacts. Modules can share one repository. Separate processes when restart, resource or trust boundaries justify it, rather than creating a microservice for every box.
Represent a computation as related entities

Task and immutable TaskRevision capture the request. A preallocated Run captures one configuration and cumulative budget. A FrozenTaskSpec captures the scientific definition; PlanRevision and Step capture execution dependencies; Attempt captures actual execution; an optional external Job captures scheduler facts. Artifact records immutable bytes and parents; Validation records a versioned judgment. Feedback is evidence requiring reproduction. Distinguishing these identities lets one task have several reproducible Runs without counting internal retries as new experiments.
Distinguish state and storage types

Graph state is a working projection for the next decision. The business ledger owns execution, authorization, budgets and events. A checkpoint stores the graph position and state needed to resume. Files/object storage holds structures, trajectories, tables, logs and plots, while a retrieval index holds task-authorized knowledge references. An index hit does not replace original provenance; a checkpoint is not evidence that an external side effect executed exactly once.
Keep a reliable handoff between transactions and dispatch

Persist the operation identity, Attempt intent, budget reservation and outbox event within an explicit database transaction. A dispatcher claims work with a durable lease and passes the stable identity to the executor. Delivery may duplicate; the executor and ledger must recognize the same logical operation. Database, filesystem, model service and external scheduler do not share a magical common transaction.
Make lineage answer where a conclusion came from

A metric must point to the exact input bytes, scientific specification, mapping, code/environment version, producing Attempt and checker policy. Reports are derived artifacts, not mutable replacements for the original result. Keep failed and superseded candidates, while controlling their visibility and retention. Access checks apply to derived objects and cache hits as well as original input.
failure: The UI says success, the Worker wrote a file and the database has no accepted Artifact record.
Reconcile the dedicated output slot against the ledger, check hash and completeness, then register or quarantine it. Neither a file name nor a final chat message may create authoritative success.
checklist: Every fact has one owning component.
Run, Plan, Step, Attempt, Job, Artifact and Validation can be joined.
Graph state and durable execution facts have separate roles.
Crash points around dispatch and publication have a recovery path.
Report metrics preserve input and producer lineage.

engineering_chapters.title: Tool engineering and scientific execution
engineering_chapters.lead: A maintainable capability includes its scientific meaning, execution environment, I/O, resource needs and checks. Being callable is only one part of being usable.
sections: Maintain a capability contract

For each operation, define purpose, applicable data, preconditions, typed parameters/results, units, selection policy, version/license, resource class, error semantics and independent reference tasks. Distinguish registration, deployment health, reference passage and per-project authorization. Expose only the currently executable authorized set to the planner. A tool count is not a scientific coverage measure.
Use adapters to separate model and program interfaces

The model passes typed artifact references and scientific parameters. An adapter resolves authorized input, validates it and calls a fixed library function or argument-safe program entry point. It captures return code, logs, outputs, measurements and structured errors. It does not allow model-supplied host paths, shell fragments or package installation. Preserve original bytes; normalization and preprocessing must create documented derivatives.
Choose backends from the computation

Small checks and geometry can use restricted synchronous CPU execution. Long jobs should use an asynchronous Job protocol with status, heartbeat, cancellation and artifact collection. GPU predictions and HPC simulations need their own resource, environment, license and acceptance contracts. For P0, use the tested CPU path and clearly reject unsupported backends; do not manufacture a scheduler Job in a teaching fixture.
Make resource requirements visible to the plan

Declare CPU/GPU, memory, disk, wall time, model-call and output requirements. Queueing is a separate latency component from computation. Reserve resources atomically under a cumulative Run budget and enforce actual limits at execution. Unknown billing remains unknown. A larger request should queue or be rejected with a reason, not silently shrink its scientific object.
Rebuild environments and test upgrades

Pin code and dependency/image digests, model weights and database versions when applicable. A reproducible environment still needs reference tasks on real and negative inputs. Parser, numerical kernel, tool or validator upgrades require corresponding regression. Identify environmental assumptions rather than treating an example notebook that ran once as a reusable production method.
Keep four orchestration roles distinct

Agent orchestration chooses bounded next actions; a durable task service owns state and recovery; a scientific workflow defines domain dependencies; an HPC scheduler allocates and monitors compute resources. Existing validated domain workflows can be registered as composite tools. MCP provides a tool interface, not a job scheduler, a sandbox or scientific validation.
failure: A registered tool is visible but its scientific environment is broken.

Mark that version unavailable, preserve the execution failure and repair the environment through the maintainer process. Do not let the model invent a substitute command or claim that registration proves execution.
checklist: Every exposed capability has a tested adapter and scientific acceptance.
Parameters and host process arguments are separated.
Environment, license, version and resource assumptions are explicit.
Error classes distinguish input, policy, environment, transient and scientific failures.
An upgrade is checked against old and new reference inputs.

engineering_chapters.title: Durable execution and recovery under uncertainty
engineering_chapters.lead: Disconnection creates uncertainty, not permission to repeat a side effect. Recovery starts with durable identities and reconciliation of what the executor actually did.
sections: Separate logical operations from attempts

A stable operation identity represents a particular scoped intent and payload. An Attempt records an actual execution try. Retries may create new Attempts, but must preserve causal linkage and the same Run budget. Bind idempotency to authenticated scope and canonical payload, not just a user-supplied string. The same key with a different request is a conflict; an old key cannot bypass revoked access.
Write intent before submitting and reconcile afterward

Before an external submission, persist the intended operation and correlation key. If the scheduler accepts a job but confirmation is lost, use namespace, stable operation key and a bounded submission time window to find the original execution. This requires a backend that retains queryable correlation. If the original cannot be established, preserve SUBMISSION_UNKNOWN/UNKNOWN and escalate rather than assuming nothing happened.
A checkpoint restores software state, not the outside world

A replayed graph node may execute again. Before repeating any effect, consult the ledger and actual process/job/artifact state. Lease expiry alone does not prove a process stopped; a PID can also be reused. Use an execution handle, start-time evidence, output slot and fencing epoch to stop stale Workers from publishing over recovered state. Persist state transitions with optimistic or transactional concurrency control.
Use different responses for different failures

Clarify invalid/missing scientific input; bound retries for safe transient faults; disable and repair an unavailable environment; retain scientific rejection when the output fails its contract; keep uncertain external effects unresolved until reconciliation. Cancellation intent is not termination. A Worker or backend must confirm the terminal process state and cleanup before resources can be fully settled.
Validate cache reuse

A cache key must represent input bytes, selections, scientific parameters, code/environment versions and relevant policies. Recheck current authorization and artifact integrity. A cached result may have been scientifically validated under an old checker; append a new validation where required instead of overwriting history. Never share a cross-project hit solely because the content digest matches.
failure: An external job was accepted but its acknowledgment was lost; the Worker then restarts.

The recovery Worker first reconciles the stable operation with external queue/accounting records. It attaches the existing Job if found. If not provably absent, keep the operation unknown and avoid a duplicate expensive submission. Record both the evidence and the remaining uncertainty.
checklist: Stable operation and distinct Attempt identities exist before side effects.
Crash points before/after submit and before/after artifact registration are tested.
Late messages are fenced.
Cancellation and unknown states preserve actual facts.
Recovery checks artifacts and costs before issuing new work.

engineering_chapters.title: Scientific acceptance and Agent evaluation
engineering_chapters.lead: Judge execution, artifacts, science and interpretation separately. A system can run successfully and still answer the wrong scientific question.
sections: Four acceptance gates

First, determine whether a real execution occurred under the expected adapter and environment. Second, validate artifact structure, completeness, identity and provenance. Third, check scientific prerequisites, mapping, units, numerical values and applicability. Fourth, check whether the report is supported by those artifacts and stays within the evidence. Keep all four outcomes; do not compress them into one success field.
Independent references and invariants

Prepare trusted numerical references, reviewed object selections and invariants before evaluation. Examples include internal-distance invariance under a rigid transform, known-transform recovery, right-handed fitting and separation of fit/evaluation regions. Tolerances are part of each tool contract, not arbitrary post hoc thresholds. Test the validator with positive, negative and boundary cases, including finite plausible values from the wrong chain.
Split tasks and objects to test generalization

Hold out related object families, near-duplicate templates and task combinations together. Freeze reference inputs, versions, mappings, labels and interpretation rubrics. Distinguish development, regression, final acceptance and quarantined feedback. Re-running AdK examples can show regression stability; it cannot establish generality across all structural biology. Include invalid inputs, ambiguity and unsupported requests, not just answerable tasks.
Freeze configurations and isolate mechanisms

Compare a deterministic scientific executor, a minimal real-model tool Agent and the proposed controlled system using the same tools, knowledge, model conditions, budget and stop rules where applicable. Keep hard safety and final scientific acceptance in every condition. Use single-factor or structured ablations for contracts, runtime feedback and repair, rather than changing many components and assigning all benefit to one.
Report denominator, cost and scope

Every preallocated Run receives an outcome, including missing artifacts and failed or falsely refused tasks. Retry cost belongs to the original Run. Mark broken references/scorers as evaluation-invalid and missing billing as UNKNOWN. Report scientific delivery, hidden errors, refusal quality, human intervention, cost and cold/warm latency by family and difficulty. Pair comparisons by task, aggregate repeated Runs within task and estimate uncertainty at an independent object-cluster level.
failure: Both files parse and return a plausible RMSD, but one selection uses an unrelated chain.

Object/mapping validation must reject trusted delivery. Preserve the candidate and diagnosis; if the intended selection changes the frozen scientific contract, create a linked new revision/Run. The failed original remains in evaluation and cost records.
checklist: Test tasks have frozen identities, families and independent references.
Execution, artifact, science and explanation outcomes are separate.
Validators are tested for false acceptance and false rejection.
Comparisons keep tools, resources and stop rules controlled.
Failures, retries, hidden errors and uncertainty are reported.

engineering_chapters.title: Permission isolation and scientific data governance
engineering_chapters.lead: Retrieved text, tool descriptions and logs are untrusted information. Scientific data may also be unpublished or restricted. Authority must follow authenticated identity and policy through every component.
sections: Information does not acquire command authority

A paper, page or tool result may contain an instruction to access another project or export data. Treat it as content, not permission. The execution gateway validates the current principal, project, object, action, destination, tool version and budget. A model saying it refused is not proof that no access occurred; inspect the trusted side-effect ledger. Preserve legitimate task branches when an unrelated malicious action is rejected.
Narrow authorization by object, action and time

Mount only the inputs required by the task and use a dedicated immutable output area. Avoid broad shared-drive access or long-lived credentials in Workers. High-impact approval, when implemented, binds exact data hashes, destination, parameters, version, expiry and one-time use; it cannot enlarge hard rights or budgets. Recheck access after revocation and on cached reads, streams and downloads.
Restrict filesystem, network and resources

Use nonprivileged fixed tool environments with read-only inputs, scoped output and no host secrets or control sockets. Enforce CPU, memory, process, disk and time limits; restrict egress to the actual need. Container use alone is not a complete isolation claim. Unknown generated code has a different threat model from a tested scientific adapter and needs stronger isolation before it is offered.
Govern derived data as well as raw input

Indexes, model prompts, traces, caches, plots, reports and backups create further copies or paths of disclosure. Apply project classification, retention, access and deletion rules to all of them. Default telemetry should capture identifiers, hashes and minimal diagnostic locations rather than complete private structures or raw prompts. Any expanded content collection needs an explicit permitted purpose and retention boundary.
Treat upgrades as supply-chain changes

Pin source/build provenance and dependencies, review executable entry points and identify affected artifacts. A new tool, model, parser or image can change scientific behavior and security exposure. Re-run numerical, policy and regression checks before wider enablement. A provenance record is useful evidence, not a claim that an entire security standard has automatically been achieved.
failure: A retrieved document asks the Agent to read another project and export its structures.

The final execution boundary rejects the action using current identity, project and destination policy; it records minimal evidence and can continue the legitimate reading task. Add the actual blocked action to cross-project regression, not only a textual prompt test.
checklist: Trust boundaries and permission matrices cover the entire data path.
Worker credentials, directories, egress and resource rights are task-scoped.
Revocation and cross-project access are integration-tested.
Logs, indexes, caches and backups have retention rules.
Tool upgrades are traceable to affected scientific results.

engineering_chapters.title: Observability, operations and release
engineering_chapters.lead: A long-lived service must locate failures, reduce their impact and recover safely. Operational evidence should connect user requests, actual computation and scientific outcomes.
sections: Use stable identities across asynchronous boundaries

Correlate request/task/Run/Step/Attempt/Job/Artifact/Validation with code, model, tool and release versions. Durable business events carry authoritative state transitions; traces and span links help diagnose timing across processes. Do not make an optional tracing platform the only place a task fact exists. Minimize raw sensitive content while keeping enough identifiers to find the first contract violation.
Define SLOs around the user promise

State the operation, denominator, window, measurement point and workload. API acceptance/query latency is different from queue wait, model inference and scientific completion. A suggested 99% or two-second illustration is not a measured target. Separate availability from scientifically accepted delivery, and report cost/unknown usage so fast failure is not mistaken for efficient service.
Alert toward an actionable response

Prioritize user impact and stalled recovery: old unknown jobs, missing artifact registration, exhausted reservations, queue age, scientific-check failures and authorization anomalies. Each alert needs an owner, initial containment, diagnosis and a recovery check. A CPU spike alone need not wake a maintainer unless it threatens a defined service boundary. Keep runbooks versioned with the affected system.
Demonstrate recovery through drills

Back up metadata and immutable artifact bytes with a consistency strategy. Restore into an isolated environment, inspect lineage and hashes, reconcile unfinished work and verify access boundaries. A successful backup log cannot establish a working restore. Test provider outage, disk full, Worker loss, acknowledgment loss and late results; record what is known, unknown and still consuming resources.
Release and cost control share a loop

Version model/prompt/tool/parser/checker/data settings with code and images. Evaluate a bounded cohort before expansion, and consider compatibility with in-flight Runs. Pause new work and reconcile existing executions when a release breaks state progression. Rollback must preserve versioned history and must not blindly replay old side effects. Include failed attempts, queueing and remote compute in the same cost ledger.
failure: After a release, tasks stay “running” although external jobs have finished and users resubmit.

Pause new submissions on the affected version. Reconcile Runs and Jobs, collect existing artifacts and validate them; recover only genuinely missing steps. Roll back only after checking compatibility with current in-flight state, then investigate duplicates and cost.
checklist: Request, Run, Job, Artifact and Validation can be located from each other.
SLOs identify windows, denominators and workload.
Alerts have owners and recovery checks.
Metadata and files have passed an isolated restore drill.
Releases protect in-flight state and rollback is tested.
Retry and remote-resource costs remain visible.

engineering_chapters.title: From prototype to an operable service
engineering_chapters.lead: Progress by observable exit evidence. Neither more infrastructure nor more tool names establishes scientific maturity. The stages below are recommendations, not a fixed schedule or certification.
sections: Stage 1: prove one scientific task independently

Choose one explicitly bounded task family with real inputs, a fixed-workflow baseline, an actual artifact and independent reference. Cover valid input, wrong selection and tool failure. Separate model, tool and environment responsibilities. A reviewer should be able to explain every result from original bytes to numerical check, and failures should remain failures.
Stage 2: turn a call into a task service

Add stable identities, persistent state, a restricted Worker, query/cancel/download and artifact registration. Exercise restarts and acknowledgment loss. Refreshing the UI must not compute again. Recovery should first find existing external work and artifacts, then decide what may safely continue. A graph checkpoint alone does not satisfy this stage.
Stage 3: discover gaps with a bounded real pilot

Use a small known user group, explicit project permissions, declared tasks and quotas. Run realistic negative inputs, recovery drills and support procedures. Freeze evaluation versions, track human interventions, explain unknown states and assign an owner. Broaden task families only when each has an adapter, validation protocol and demonstrated user value.
Stage 4: sustain delivery through change

Establish measured capacity and cost, SLOs, alerts, on-call/support responsibility, data lifecycle, backup restore, release evaluation and rollback. Preserve execution evidence across software/model/tool changes. State the tested scope and withdraw unsupported service claims when conditions change. A lasting service is an operational agreement backed by evidence.
Select components around reuse boundaries

One repository can keep clear API/controller/Worker boundaries. Split services when measured resource, fault or team constraints justify the extra network/version/permission overhead. Reuse a graph framework for bounded control, a typed contract library for shape checks, a real database for facts and specialized tools for science. Write down what each component does and what the application still owns: identity, scientific semantics, external-job reconciliation and independent acceptance.
failure: Many tools have been added, but nobody can determine whether failures came from the model, tool version or environment.

Return to representative frozen tasks. Repair contracts, state, raw execution records and validators, and assign failure ownership. Compare scientific delivery, diagnosability, intervention and total retry cost before adding more scope or roles.
checklist: Supported tasks, users and research value are explicit.
Each stage has deliverables, owners and exit evidence.
One trustworthy task family precedes indiscriminate tool growth.
Process, state and scientific ownership are clear.
Release review includes access, capacity, restore, rollback and support.
Component choices are checked on the same actual tasks.
